title: Prime-pair charts of the principal w-localization
statement: For a commutative ring A and its principal w-localization W [def-weil-pbc-w-localization], there is a bijection e between Spec W [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and pairs (x,y) of primes of A with y contained in x. Contraction along A -> W is the second coordinate. The first-coordinate map is continuous for the patch topology [def-weil-pbc-w-local] on Spec A. For each prime x, the explicit evaluation rho_x: W -> A_x [lem-weil-pbc-principal-w-localization-evaluation] induces a closed immersion Spec A_x -> Spec W whose image is exactly the first-coordinate fibre at x.

proof.text: For each prime q of W and stage i, Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.sigmaToPi_bijective decomposes its contracted prime into a unique factor E_i and a prime of A_{f_i,E_i}. Compatibility of the injections makes selected parts refine each other.

The selected parts are nonempty closed sets in the patch spectrum. A common refinement gives directedness. Mathlib compactness of WithConstructibleTopology (PrimeSpectrum A), together with the directed compact-intersection lemma, gives x in every selected part. For f outside x, use the D(f),V(f) cut with denominator f on D(f). That factor inverts f, so f is outside y=q cap A. Hence y is contained in x.

For y contained in x define q_(x,y) as the inverse image under rho_x of the prime of A_x corresponding to y by the localization prime order isomorphism. Its contraction to A is y and its selected part at each stage contains x. Primes of a principal localization are determined by contraction; thus selected parts and y determine every stage contraction. Every element of W has a stage representative, so these data determine q. This proves surjectivity of the pair construction.

For constructible E use the cut by E and its complement, both denominators 1, and take the characteristic tuple. Its image in W evaluates to 1 at x in E and 0 outside E. Thus D of this element detects membership of the first coordinate in E. Taking E=D(f) distinguishes distinct first coordinates, and contraction distinguishes second coordinates. The pair construction is therefore bijective.

Every patch subbasic set is constructible. Its inverse image under the first-coordinate map is the basic open of its characteristic element. The generating-topology criterion proves continuity to the patch spectrum.

The evaluation map rho_x is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-principal-w-localization-evaluation], so Mathlib IsClosedImmersion.spec_of_surjective makes Spec A_x -> Spec W a closed immersion. The localization prime order isomorphism and the pair bijection identify its image with precisely the first-coordinate fibre at x.

lean.statement:
theorem primeCharts (A : Type u) [CommRing A] :
    ∃ e : PrimeSpectrum (algebra A) ≃
      {p : PrimeSpectrum A × PrimeSpectrum A // p.2.asIdeal ≤ p.1.asIdeal},
      (∀ q, PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A (algebra A)) q = (e q).val.2) ∧
      (@Continuous (PrimeSpectrum (algebra A)) (PrimeSpectrum A) inferInstance
        (constructibleTopology (PrimeSpectrum A)) (fun q ↦ (e q).val.1)) ∧
      (∀ x : PrimeSpectrum A,
        ∃ ρ : algebra A →ₐ[A] Localization.AtPrime x.asIdeal,
          IsClosedImmersion (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ρ.toRingHom)) ∧
          Set.range (PrimeSpectrum.comap ρ.toRingHom) = {q | (e q).val.1 = x})
